rebecca holy. Good morning. good morning, chair randall and members of the board. I want to acknowledge board members, staff, volunteers, community partners, and survivors who are with us in the room and online today. I am samantha clark, the ceo of domestic violence and sexual assault services. Loudoun county has long been a leader in supporting victims of domestic violence and sexual assault. For years loudoun has been at the forefront of providing trauma survivors services. Our success

is rooted in strong partnerships between the county, law-enforcement, courts, schools, and many other community-based organizations. This coordinated approach works. Last year alone, provided 88 adults and 31 children knights of emergency shelter. 743 survivors received more than 4000 hours of assistance, and 1183 hotline calls were answered. We prioritize safety and well-being of children, providing 307 hours of trauma therapy, 144 forensic interviews for child victims, and violence

prevention education for more than 1600 youth and youth serving professionals. These numbers reflect services expertly delivered and lives saved, families stabilized, and cycles of violence disrupted. Survivors in loudoun county know where to turn for trusted services and resources, and help come because of the system that has been carefully built over four decades between law, community organizations, and the

county, to prioritize safety and healing. The shared goal of law and the county has always been to ensure that survivors receive care without barriers, delays, or fragmentation. As the county considers funding proposed to develop countywide survivor services and coordination, I ask you to consider the enormous opportunity to build upon the strong foundation we have forged

together. As the ceo, I want you to know that we are capable and ready to leverage years of collective experience and institutional knowledge to shape a well coordinated survivor centric approach with you. We are equally and fully committed to standing with the county to help ensure that any new initiatives enhance and reinforce this existing network of care. Loudoun survivors response is strongest when

services are aligned, and survivor access is seamless. Laws is eager to work alongside loudoun county and our valuable community partners. Together we can make sure that loudoun remains a leader in compassionate, effective care, setting a standard for communities across the county. Thank you. thank you, and thank you to everyone involved to do such important work. Rebecca, followed by breanna carr, followed by diana rodriguez. Good morning.
